answer:
**Best estimate:** **3.1 million units sold** of **HARBOE CSD in Danish retail in 2026-01**.

**Plausible range:** **2.1 million–4.8 million units**.  
**Confidence:** **Low-to-moderate, ~35%** — public sources give market/category and Harboe position clues, but not internal SKU-level unit sales.

**How I estimated it:**
- Public evidence says Danish soft-drink sales were large and growing: DTU/Euromonitor reported **966m liters of soft drinks in Denmark in 2025**, with retail/off-trade accounting for most sales; for **sodavand/CSD**, the report notes retail is **80%** of sales. ([food.dtu.dk](https://www.food.dtu.dk/-/media/institutter/foedevareinstituttet/publikationer/pub-2025/markeds-og-vareundersoegelse-af-energidrikke-i-danmark-final-report.pdf))
- Harboe reported a **soft-drinks value share of 8.1%** in Danish retail in MAT week 20 2025, and said **54% of Danes bought** Harboe soft drinks or Apollinaris in 2024. ([investor.harboes.com](https://investor.harboes.com/static-files/88ec4164-f72a-4d68-95b6-f85bb8680432))
- Harboe’s 2025/26 report says Denmark beverage volume grew **14%**, its Danish market-share trend remained positive, and soft drinks in Denmark grew **2.6%** over the past year; it also describes Harboe as broadly represented across Danish retail and positioned in the lower-price segment. ([harboes.gcs-web.com](https://harboes.gcs-web.com/static-files/5b7da5bb-a45d-42fa-8a08-d0154dae2c44))
- I converted Harboe’s **8.1% value share** to an estimated **~11–12% volume share** because Harboe is lower-priced, assumed January is a seasonally weak CSD month at **~6.8% of annual volume**, and assumed an average retail “unit” of about **1.1 liters** across large PET bottles, 0.5L bottles, cans, and multipacks.
